nodes.summary: If `f` is an `(L, C)`- and `g` an `(L', C')`-quasi-isometry, then `g ∘ f` is an `(L' L, L' C + 2 C')`-quasi-isometry.
nodes.title: Composition of quasi-isometries

nodes.summary: If `f` is an `(L, C)`- and `g` an `(L', C')`-quasi-isometric embedding, then `g ∘ f` is an `(L' L, L' C + C')`-quasi-isometric embedding.
nodes.title: Composition of quasi-isometric embeddings

nodes.summary: An `(L, C)`-quasi-isometric embedding satisfies `d(x, y) ≤ L (d(f x, f y) + C)`.
nodes.title: Lower bound of a quasi-isometric embedding

nodes.summary: An `(L, C)`-quasi-isometric embedding satisfies `d(f x, f y) ≤ L d(x, y) + C`.
nodes.title: Upper bound of a quasi-isometric embedding

nodes.summary: An $(L, C)$-quasi-isometry $f : X \to Y$ has a quasi-inverse: an $(L, 3LC)$-quasi-isometry $g : Y \to X$ with $d(f(g y), y) \le C$ and $d(g(f x), x) \le 2LC$ for all $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Quasi-inverse of a quasi-isometry

nodes.title: Quasi-isometric embedding

nodes.summary: An $(L, C)$-quasi-isometry $f : X \to Y$ is an $(L, C)$-quasi-isometric embedding whose image is $C$-dense: every $y \in Y$ is within distance $C$ of some $f x$. The second condition is what makes quasi-isometry symmetric: a quasi-isometry has a quasi-inverse.
nodes.title: Quasi-isometry

nodes.summary: An `(L, C)`-quasi-isometry is an `(L', C')`-quasi-isometry whenever `L ≤ L'` and `C ≤ C'`.
nodes.title: Weakening the constants of a quasi-isometry

nodes.summary: An `(L, C)`-quasi-isometric embedding is an `(L', C')`-quasi-isometric embedding whenever `L ≤ L'` and `C ≤ C'`.
nodes.title: Weakening the constants of a quasi-isometric embedding

nodes.summary: Two pseudometric spaces $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-isometric if there is an $(L, C)$-quasi-isometry $X \to Y$ for some constants $L$ and $C$. This is an equivalence relation (reflexive, symmetric by the quasi-inverse, transitive by composition), and it is the equivalence under which Gromov studies the large-scale geometry of finitely generated groups: the invariants of a group that matter are those of its quasi-isometry…
nodes.title: Quasi-isometric spaces

nodes.summary: Every pseudometric space is quasi-isometric to itself.
nodes.title: Quasi-isometry is reflexive

nodes.summary: If `X` is quasi-isometric to `Y`, then `Y` is quasi-isometric to `X`.
nodes.title: Quasi-isometry is symmetric

nodes.summary: If `X` is quasi-isometric to `Y` and `Y` to `Z`, then `X` is quasi-isometric to `Z`.
nodes.title: Quasi-isometry is transitive

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
